title: The Empty Half of the Market
summaryZh: 娜迪雅在週三市場賣了十九年的菜。環城路上的超市開了兩年之後,四十個攤位只剩十一個。這天她第一次走進那間超市。

sentences.text: Nadia had sold vegetables in the Wednesday market for nineteen years.
sentences.zh: 娜迪雅在週三市場賣菜已經十九年了。

sentences.text: Her stall stood in the same corner, under the same green roof, every single week.
sentences.zh: 她的攤位每個星期都在同一個角落、同一片綠色屋頂底下。

sentences.text: When she started, there were forty stalls and the aisles were hard to walk through.
sentences.zh: 她剛開始擺攤時有四十個攤位,走道擠得幾乎走不過去。

sentences.text: This morning she counted them again and stopped at eleven.
sentences.zh: 今天早上她又數了一次,數到十一就沒了。

sentences.text: The supermarket on the ring road had opened two winters ago.
sentences.zh: 環城路上那間超市是兩個冬天前開的。

sentences.text: It was warm inside, it stayed open until ten at night, and it had a car park.
sentences.zh: 裡面很暖和,開到晚上十點,而且有停車場。

sentences.text: One by one, the other sellers had stopped coming.
sentences.zh: 其他攤商一個接一個不再來了。

sentences.text: The fish man went first, then the bread woman, then the brothers who sold cheese.
sentences.zh: 先是賣魚的,接著是賣麵包的太太,然後是賣起司的兄弟倆。

sentences.text: Each of them had said the same thing on the way out: I am sorry, Nadia.
sentences.zh: 他們每個人離開時說的都是同一句話:對不起,娜迪雅。

sentences.text: Nadia kept her prices low and her tomatoes better than anybody else's.
sentences.zh: 娜迪雅價格壓得很低,番茄也比誰家的都好。

sentences.text: None of it had been anything like enough.
sentences.zh: 這些完全不夠。

sentences.text: Her son Karim came to help her pack up at noon.
sentences.zh: 中午時,她兒子卡林來幫她收攤。

sentences.text: He was twenty-four and he worked with numbers at an insurance office.
sentences.zh: 他二十四歲,在一間保險公司做數字相關的工作。

sentences.text: "You could sell online," he said, for the third Wednesday in a row.
sentences.zh: 「你可以在網路上賣啊,」他說。這已經是連續第三個星期三了。

sentences.text: "Photographs, a delivery van, a website. I could build all of it for you."
sentences.zh: 「拍照、送貨車、一個網站。這些我都可以幫你弄。」

sentences.text: Nadia looked at the eleven stalls and the wide empty spaces between them.
sentences.zh: 娜迪雅看著那十一個攤位,還有攤位之間空蕩蕩的大片空地。

sentences.text: "And then who would I talk to?" she said.
sentences.zh: 「那我要跟誰講話?」她說。

sentences.text: Karim did not have an answer for that one, and he did not pretend to.
sentences.zh: 這個問題卡林答不上來,他也沒有假裝答得上來。

sentences.text: He carried the crates out to the van and said nothing more about websites.
sentences.zh: 他把箱子搬上車,沒有再提網站的事。

sentences.text: That night Nadia sat at her kitchen table and did the arithmetic properly.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上,娜迪雅坐在廚房桌前,認真把帳算了一遍。

sentences.text: If Wednesdays stayed like this until winter, she would have to stop.
sentences.zh: 如果星期三一直是這樣到冬天,她就得收了。

sentences.text: She wrote the last number at the bottom of the page and drew a line beneath it.
sentences.zh: 她把最後一個數字寫在頁面底端,在下面畫了一條線。

sentences.text: On Thursday she drove out to the supermarket on the ring road.
sentences.zh: 星期四,她開車去了環城路上那間超市。

sentences.text: In two years she had never once walked through its doors.
sentences.zh: 開了兩年,她一次也沒有走進去過。

sentences.text: The tomatoes were stacked in a perfect red wall, and they cost less than hers.
sentences.zh: 番茄堆成一面完美的紅色牆,價錢還比她的便宜。

sentences.text: She stood in the aisle for a long time, holding one of them.
sentences.zh: 她在走道上站了很久,手裡拿著一顆。

sentences.text: It was heavy and cold in her hand, and it had no smell at all.
sentences.zh: 拿在手裡沉甸甸的、冰冰的,一點味道也沒有。

sentences.text: Then she noticed the woman beside her, also holding a tomato, also not moving.
sentences.zh: 然後她注意到旁邊那位太太,也拿著一顆番茄,也一動不動。

sentences.text: It was Mrs. Haddad, who had bought from Nadia every Wednesday for eleven years.
sentences.zh: 那是哈達太太,十一年來每個星期三都跟娜迪雅買菜。

sentences.text: They looked at each other and neither of them spoke for a moment.
sentences.zh: 兩人對望著,一時之間誰也沒開口。

sentences.text: "My daughter drives me here now," Mrs. Haddad said. "It is easier for her."
sentences.zh: 「現在是我女兒載我來的,」哈達太太說。「這樣她比較方便。」

sentences.text: Nadia put the tomato back on the perfect red wall.
sentences.zh: 娜迪雅把番茄放回那面完美的紅色牆上。

sentences.text: She walked out of the supermarket without buying a single thing.
sentences.zh: 她什麼都沒買就走出了超市。

sentences.text: On the way home she did not think about prices, or websites, or empty stalls.
sentences.zh: 回家的路上,她想的不是價格、網站,也不是空掉的攤位。

sentences.text: She thought about how long Mrs. Haddad had stood there, holding a tomato she did not want.
sentences.zh: 她想的是哈達太太站在那裡多久,手裡拿著一顆她根本不想要的番茄。

sentences.text: By the time she reached her own street, Nadia had the beginning of an idea.
sentences.zh: 回到自己那條街時,娜迪雅心裡已經有了一個想法的開頭。

sentences.text: It was not a good idea yet, and it was not finished, but it was hers.
sentences.zh: 那還算不上一個好想法,也還沒完整,但那是她自己的。

questions.q: What has happened to the Wednesday market over the years?
options: It has shrunk from forty stalls to eleven
It has moved to a warmer building with a car park
It has started opening until ten at night

questions.q: Why does Nadia refuse her son's idea of selling online?
options: It would leave her with nobody to talk to
She does not believe her tomatoes would sell
The delivery van would cost more than she earns

questions.q: What does Nadia realise while watching Mrs. Haddad?
options: Her old customer is not happy shopping there either
Her own tomatoes are no longer good enough
Her prices will have to come down again
